stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 2 x^{2} - 16 x + 24 \) and \( g(x) = 0 \). Find the exact total area of the regions between the graphs of f and g from \( x = 1 \) to \( x = \frac{13}{2} \).

worked_solution.text: \( f(x) - g(x) = 2 \left(x - 6\right) \left(x - 2\right) \), so the graphs cross at \( x = 2 \) and \( x = 6 \), both inside the interval. f is above g before the first crossing and after the second, and below g between them.
worked_solution.rule_named: intersections and order of the curves

worked_solution.text: The pieces are \( \int_{1}^{2} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{14}{3} \), \( \int_{2}^{6} \left(g(x) - f(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{64}{3} \) and \( \int_{6}^{\frac{13}{2}} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{13}{12} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: area of each piece, upper minus lower

worked_solution.text: The total area is the sum of the pieces, \( \frac{325}{12} \).

options.derivation: the curves split correctly but each piece integrated as lower minus upper
f(x) - g(x) integrated once over the whole interval, across both crossings
the crossing at x = 6 missed, so the second integral runs from 2 to 13/2 across it
